title: K Composition Rules — How K Combines Across Systems

KC-2.note: FP coupling: harmonic (coupled regime). Info theory: multiplicative at MI=0 (ratio=1.0000), sub-multiplicative under correlation. INTERPRETATION: composition rule depends on coupling regime. This is physically consistent but means no single universal rule.

KC-3.description: K_eff monotonically increasing in K_A and K_B
KC-3.analysis: Violations occur even at lambda=0 (16 violations). When K_A << K_B, the mixture density is bimodal (sharp B-peak + broad A-hill). The variance of this bimodal mixture exceeds that of a unimodal Eckert density at moderate Pe, so variance-matched K_eff decreases. This is not a pathology of K but a limitation of the mixture-density approach: two very asymmetric uncoupled systems do not have a single effective K. K composition is only well-defined for systems in the same regime.

KC-5.description: K_eff = K when K_A = K_B = K (lambda=0)

test2_information_theory.conclusion: Independent systems: K multiplicative (tensor product). Correlated systems: K sub-multiplicative. K_eff ~ K_A * K_B * exp(-gamma * MI) with fitted gamma.

test3_llm_scaling.conclusion: INCONCLUSIVE. K and C are confounded in HP192 data. Pe variation comes from behavioral dimension mapping, not DOF count. Need independent C estimation to separate K.

test5_coarse_graining.conclusion: K_eff (entropy-based) monotonically decreases under coarse-graining. K is a resolution-dependent quantity. Scaling: K_eff ~ K_nominal^beta with beta in [0.6, 1.0] depending on distribution shape.

synthesis.main_finding: NO single universal composition rule. K composition depends on the coupling regime and system similarity. (1) EQUAL SYSTEMS (K_A=K_B): K_eff = K exactly at lambda=0 (KC-5 PASS, <0.001% error). With coupling, K_eff decreases toward K*(1-f(lambda)). (2) SIMILAR SYSTEMS: harmonic mean is best single predictor (R^2=0.978 across all lambda, slope~1.0). (3) ASYMMETRIC SYSTEMS (K_A << K_B): combined K is pulled toward the SMALLER system. The mixture density is bimodal, and no single K characterizes it — K_eff is dominated by the less constrained component. (4) INFORMATION THEORY: independent systems are multiplicative (K_AB = K_A*K_B, tensor product), with sub-multiplicative reduction under correlation (K_eff ~ K_A*K_B*exp(-1.12*MI), R^2=0.79). (5) COARSE-GRAINING: K_eff monotonically decreases, tracking resolution (K_eff ~ K^beta, beta in [0.6,1.0]).
synthesis.implications: K-Factorization (SS136) is preserved: shape factors Q_shape(O,R,alpha) are K-independent because the mixture dominance by the less-constrained component is a K-level effect that does not alter the ratio structure. K composition being regime-dependent explains why K remains external in the RG flow (HP206): it is not a running coupling but a resolution-dependent DOF count. The harmonic mean dominance in the coupled regime connects to HP207 (pairwise Pe): K_eff = K_A*K_B/(K_A+K_B) = harmonic/2 is exactly the reduced mass formula from classical mechanics, suggesting K functions as an effective mass in the Pe dynamics. The key physical lesson: coupling constraints reduce effective DOF (sub-additive), while independent DOF multiply (tensor product). There is no single composition law because the structure of the interaction determines which regime applies.
